messages.author: f56d4c6b6451e734
messages.subject: Save result of compileNimble() as .Rdata
parts:
Good afternoon,

I am trying to save the result of compileNimble() to access later. For example, if I run the following code, and then try to load the file, I get an error that I think is associated with the binding: "Error in .Call(NULL, <pointer: (nil)>) : first argument must be a string (of length 1) or native symbol reference".

Is there a certain way I can save this as an .Rdata file or a different type of file?

Thank you for your time!

My code:
Rmodel <- nimbleModel(model_string, inits = inits, constants = consts)
Rmcmc <- buildMCMC(mcmcConf, enableWAIC = TRUE)
comp_model <- compileNimble(Rmodel)
comp_MCMC <- compileNimble(Rmcmc)
comp_MCMC$run(niter = 200000)

save(comp_MCMC, file = "C:/Users/ckell/Desktop/test.Rdata")

In separate session:
load(file = "C:/Users/ckell/Desktop/test.Rdata")

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: Save result of compileNimble() as .Rdata
parts:
Sorry again for delays.  A good model of nimble developers will correctly conclude we don't have as much time to respond here as we'd like, but please keep the questions coming.

I agree matrix2mv is not very clear.  It's not even exported.  I've just filed a github issue for us to improve usability of modelValues objects.  Meanwhile, here is an example that I think should get you going.  It illustrates running an mcmc, extracting samples, then directly putting them into a new mcmc (as if you're in a new R session).  You should be able to run WAIC from there.

library(nimble)

toyModel <- nimbleModel(
    nimbleCode({
        a ~ dnorm(0,1)
        for(i in 1:2) x[i] ~ dnorm(0, 1)
    })
)

toyMCMC <- buildMCMC(toyModel)

CtoyModel <- compileNimble(toyModel)
CtoyMCMC <- compileNimble(toyMCMC, project = toyModel)
CtoyMCMC$run(50)

samples <- as.matrix(CtoyMCMC$mvSamples)
samplesList <- as.list(CtoyMCMC$mvSamples) # another way to store samples

## Illustrate use of matrix2mv to set first two rows to zero
emptySamples <- samples[1:2,]
emptySamples[1:2, 1:3] <- 0
emptySamples
# matrix2mv only resizes CtoyMCMC$mvSamples if it needs to be longer.
# It doesn't shorten it.
nimble:::matrix2mv(emptySamples, CtoyMCMC$mvSamples)
as.matrix(CtoyMCMC$mvSamples)[1:2,]

# Make a fully independent object, as if we've restarted R
toyModel2 <- nimbleModel(
    nimbleCode({
        a ~ dnorm(0,1)
        for(i in 1:2) x[i] ~ dnorm(0, 1)
    })
)

toyMCMC2 <- buildMCMC(toyModel2)
CtoyModel2 <- compileNimble(toyModel2)
CtoyMCMC2 <- compileNimble(toyMCMC2, project = toyModel2)
CtoyMCMC2$run(1) # I am adding this defensively, to run initializations
nimble:::matrix2mv(samples, CtoyMCMC2$mvSamples)
as.matrix(CtoyMCMC2$mvSamples)

messages.author: 0ef2647ddd7095d7
messages.subject: Re: Save result of compileNimble() as .Rdata
parts:
Great to hear.

I realized one tweak that could improve the speed.  When creating the MCMC that is only for the purpose of re-populating the samples and running WAIC, you can use nodes=NULL.  This will make the MCMC configuration not have any samplers, which will make it build and compile faster. In the example code I sent before, the change would be:

toyMCMC2 <- buildMCMC(toyModel2, nodes = NULL)

-Perry
